label: Google Sheets
description: Reads rows from a sheet, or appends rows to it.

params.name: columns
params.label: Columns To Send
params.hint: One row per item: the column name and the value to write.

docs.summary: Reads rows out of a spreadsheet, or appends rows to one.
docs.mode: It depends on the operation, and the node tells you which: `read` runs once and returns one item per row; `append` runs once per item and writes one row each.
docs.when: Use it as the source when the data lives in a sheet, or as the destination when a human needs to look at the result afterwards. A sheet is often the most useful output an automation can have.

params.name: operation
params.text: `read` fetches the sheet. `append` adds rows to the end of it.

params.name: columns
params.text: For `append`: one row per item, built from the column name and the value to write.

examples.label: Append one row per item

gotchas: Read gives you one item per row, already flattened — no Split Out needed afterwards.
Append runs once per item, so the number of rows written is the number of items that reached it. Check the item count on the node before blaming the sheet.
A column name you did not list is not written. There is no "everything else" shortcut.
